messages:
jordan: Need a quick follow-up from the headroom contracts RFC — trying to nail what telemetry we actually need from the operator to make autoscaling safe.
neha: Agree. We keep debating metrics at a high level but we don't have a small, actionable set.
kyle: Minimal set I care about: queue_length, ready_gpu_count, prewarm_inflight, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_load_ms.
rachel: Also add eviction_latency and warmup_time_percentile (p50/p95). We had surprises when warmup was 45s for some models.
jordan: Good call. If warmup p95 > 20s we should bias headroom higher or prefer prewarmed lanes.
neha: Question: should the operator expose derived signals (e.g., headroom_deficit = requested - available_prewarm) or do we compute that in control plane?
sam: My vote: basic primitives from operator, derived signals in control plane. Less coupling, easier operator rollback.
luis: But control plane needs timely samples. Can we push a push-metric for sporadic events (failed_load, eviction_reason)?
ops-bot: auto: new metric proposal posted to /metrics repo: redwood.dedicated.operator.headroom_events_count (type=counter)
kyle: Nice. Also would like a simple label set: pool_id, model_family, quantization, tenant_tier.
rachel: Label explosion is real — limit to pool_id/model_family/zone for cardinality control. tenant_tier only when it's a dedicated SLA dimension.
neha: We should define a compact event wire format for the operator to emit. Something like:
```
{ "ts": 7701234567, "pool_id": "gpu-pool-3", "event": "warmup_start", "model": "llama-70b-q4", "estimate_ms": 12000 }
```
This lets control plane correlate warmup start->ready.
jordan: Love that. Also include event="model_load_failed" with error codes so rollbacks can trigger.
luis: For SLOs, we need rolling windows for headroom deficit (e.g., 5m/1h) plus counts of requests that hit fallback.
sam: Fallback_count is critical for reliability alerts. Can we tag fallback by fallback_type (model_variant/region/capacity_tier)?
kyle: Implementation detail: operator should aggregate short-term (10s/1m) and emit both raw and aggregated to reduce telemetry traffic.
neha: Agree for bandwidth reasons. But also keep raw sample on disk for debugging. Export aggregated and store raw to local log for n days.
rachel: What about metric naming conventions? Use redwood.dedicated.* prefix and avoid camelCase.
jordan: Action items: 1) Draft metrics list + labels (neha) 2) Event wire schema + examples (luis) 3) Operator pseudo-code for aggregation windows (kyle) 4) SLO alert thresholds and how control plane consumes (rachel/sam)
neha: I'll sketch the list. Example minimal metrics: ["queue_length", "available_prewarm", "inflight_warmups", "warmup_p95_ms", "model_load_failures", "eviction_latency_ms", "fallback_count"]
kyle: Pseudo:
```
// every 10s
snap = sample(locator_stats)
agg10s.add(snap)
if now % 60 == 0: emit(agg10s.summary()); agg1m.roll(snap)
```
rachel: For rollout safety: operator exposes operator_version label and a health_probe metric so control plane can opt out of new operators that underreport.
luis: Nice. Also include a small checksum of event schema version so control plane can ignore older formats.
sam: One more: tenant-level spike protection. If we see a single tenant causing > X% of warmups in 1m, throttle that tenant's admission into prewarm lane. Operator needs to report per-tenant spikes (but maybe sampling only).
neha: Privacy concern — sampling ok, never full tenant ids in metrics. Use hashed_tenant_bucket label.
jordan: Thanks. This feels actionable. I'll make a short RFC follow-up with the exact JSON schema for events and the metric list. Then we can schedule a 30-min sync to agree on limits. :thumbsup:
rachel: Ping me when draft is up, I'll run it against current alerting playbook.
kyle: I'll write operator agg pseudo and a small integration test to validate event round-trip.
ops-bot: auto: meeting created: "Headroom metrics sync" 2026-03-25 10:00 UTC (invitees: jordan, neha, kyle, rachel, luis, sam)
jordan: Perfect — thanks everyone. End of thread.
